summary:
China’s 2018 was marked by major political changes, severe weather and high-profile censorship and tax cases. In March, the National People’s Congress amended the constitution to remove presidential term limits. The same month, Wang Qishan became vice president, Li Zhanshu became Congress chairman and Wang Yang became chairman of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference. North Korean leader Kim Jong-un met Xi Jinping in Beijing.

January blizzards killed 10 people across five provinces and affected more than 567,000. Tropical Storm Rumbia killed 53 in August, while Typhoon Mangkhut disrupted transport in Guangdong in September.

A Spring Festival Gala sketch drew accusations of racism in February. In May, authorities blocked Peppa Pig videos on Douyin, citing subversive content. Former official Sun Zhengcai was sentenced to life for corruption. In October, actress Fan Bingbing and her companies were ordered to pay about 883 million yuan in taxes, fines and penalties. November marked 40 years of reform and opening up with an exhibition visited by Xi. The planned Chang’e 4 lunar mission was also listed for June.
